'''Mouhamed Gueye''' ({{IPAc-en|ɡ|eɪ}} {{respell|GAY}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 17, 2024}}</ref> born 9 November 2002) is a Senegalese professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He moved to the United States as a teenager to play high school basketball at [[Prolific Prep]]. Gueye played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]] and was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first-team as a sophomore in 2023. He was selected as the 39th overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets]], but was traded to the Atlanta Hawks on draft night.

==Early life==
Gueye was raised in [[Dakar]], Senegal, as the youngest of four siblings in a sporting family.<ref name=pi>{{cite web|title=Mouhamed Gueye Q&A|url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/mouhamed-gueye|work=Prospective Insight|date=16 April 2021|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref><ref name=clark22>{{cite web|first=Colton|last=Clark|title='It's always been WSU': Mouhamed Gueye talks offseason, return to Washington State|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2022/jun/15/its-always-been-wsu-mouhamed-gueye-talks-offseason/|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=15 June 2022|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref> He has cousins who have played for the national basketball team and who played professionally in Europe.<ref name=pi/> Gueye grew up playing [[soccer]] but was encouraged by his mother to play basketball because of his height.<ref name=pi/> He credits watching his older brother play basketball as an early influence.<ref name=pi/>

==High school career==
Gueye's personal coach, Mamadou Cisse, connected him with Philippe Doherty, the head coach of Prolific Prep in [[Napa, California]].<ref name=pi/> At age 16, he moved from Dakar to the United States to enroll at Prolific Prep.<ref name=clark23>{{cite web|first=Colton|last=Clark|title='I'm focused on being a pro': Washington State post Mouhamed Gueye has sights on NBA|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/mar/29/im-focused-on-being-a-pro-washington-state-post-mo/|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=29 March 2023|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref> Gueye had never played organized basketball before playing at Prolific Prep.<ref name=pi/>

Gueye emerged as a four-star recruit and a top-50 recruit in the country.<ref name=clark23/> He completed his academic requirements early and [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2021 class before he committed to play for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]] over several other [[high-major]] offers.<ref name=clark23/><ref>{{cite web|first=Theo|last=Lawson|title=Washington State grabs commitment from Mouhamed Gueye, the highest-ranked recruit in program history|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2021/may/07/washington-state-grabs-commitment-from-mouhamed-gu/|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=7 May 2021|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
Gueye averaged 7.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and .5 assists per game during his freshman season with the Cougars in 2021–22.<ref name=clark23/> He was selected to the [[Pac-12]] all-freshman team.<ref name=clark23/> Gueye declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], but withdrew after receiving feedback from NBA teams.<ref name=clark23/> He also tested the [[transfer portal]] but elected to return to the Cougars for his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=7 June 2022 |title=Washington State's Mouhamed Gueye withdraws name from men's basketball transfer portal |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34052635 |access-date=19 May 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Gueye's role with the Cougars increased during the 2022–23 season following the departure of key pieces of their front-court.<ref name=clark23/> He also played primarily as a [[Center (basketball)|center]] instead of his natural [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position.<ref name=clark23/> Gueye was the centrepiece of the Cougars' offense with head coach [[Kyle Smith (basketball)|Kyle Smith]] reinforcing throughout the season that the team "plays through Gueye".<ref name=clark23/> On 2 February 2023, he scored a career-high 31 points against the [[2022–23 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC Trojans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ellis sparks Southern Cal past Washington State 80-70|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-basketball-southern-california-trojans-washington-state-cougars-mens-173c1c19b575c4bfbe9973824666532e|website=APNews.com|date=3 February 2023|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref> Gueye averaged 14.3 points, 8.4 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game during the 2022–23 season and was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first-team.<ref name=clark23/><ref>{{cite web|title=2022-23 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2023/3/7/2022-23-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance.aspx|website=Pac-12.com|date=7 March 2023|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref>

On 4 April 2023, Gueye declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Washington State forward Mouhamed Gueye officially declares for NBA draft|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/apr/04/washington-state-forward-mouhamed-gueye-officially/|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=4 April 2023|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref> He was invited to participate in the [[NBA draft combine]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Vincent|last=Saglimbeni|title=Former local college athletes prepare for next steps in basketball careers|url=https://www.kxly.com/news/former-local-college-athletes-prepare-for-next-steps-in-basketball-careers/article_8f648a4e-ef6d-11ed-807d-1f5f587ef478.html|website=KXLY.com|date=10 May 2023|access-date=19 May 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Atlanta Hawks (2023–present) ===
Gueye was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the second round as the 39th overall pick of the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Colton|last=Clark|title=Cougars' Mouhamed Gueye picked in second round of NBA draft, traded to Hawks|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-basketball/cougars-mouhamed-gueye-picked-in-second-round-of-nba-draft-traded-to-hawks/|work=Seattle Times|date=22 June 2023|access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref> His rights were traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] and then to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on draft night.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jamey|last=Vinnick|title=UPDATE: WSU's Mouhamed Gueye traded to Atlanta after being taken in Round 2 of NBA Draft|url=https://247sports.com/college/washington-state/article/mouhamed-gueye-nba-draft-wsu-basketball-charlotte-hornets-in-rou-211934520/|website=247Sports.com|date=23 June 2023|access-date=1 July 2023}}</ref> On 3 July 2023, Gueye signed his rookie contract with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Rookie Forward Mouhamed Gueye|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-rookie-forward-mouhamed-gueye|website=NBA.com|date=3 July 2023|access-date=11 July 2023}}</ref> However, on 12 November, he was ruled out for a month after suffering a right lower-back stress fracture,<ref>{{cite web|first=Lauren|last=Williams|title=Bufkin, Gueye to miss extended time with injuries|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-hawks/bufkin-gueye-to-miss-extended-time-with-injuries/LLCDB7CV6JCAPM6UDBF3EU64QI/|work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|date=12 November 2023|access-date=13 November 2023}}</ref> subsequently missing most of his rookie season.<ref name=hunt>{{cite web|first=Stephen|last=Hunt|title='It doesn't get better than this': Former Washington State big man Mouhamed Gueye loving the NBA, despite lack of minutes|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/apr/10/it-doesnt-get-better-than-this-former-washington-s/|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=10 April 2024|access-date=20 April 2024}}</ref> Gueye returned from his injury with several stints for the Hawks' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[College Park Skyhawks]], both as a rookie and a sophomore.<ref name=hunt/><ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 College Park Skyhawks Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/College-Park-Skyhawks/49/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 College Park Skyhawks Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/College-Park-Skyhawks/49/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 27, 2024}}</ref> He made six total appearances for Atlanta during his rookie campaign, posting averages of 4.0 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 0.7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mouhamed Gueye 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4712863/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=January 5, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 11 April 2025, Gueye recorded a career-high 18 rebounds and scored 10 points during a 124–110 win over the [[2024–25 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hawks 124-110 76ers (Apr 11, 2025) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401705739 |access-date=2025-08-02 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> He made 33 total appearances (including 28 starts) for the Hawks during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 6.0 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mouhamed Gueye 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4712863/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=January 5, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 8 November 2025, Gueye recorded a career-high 21 points with seven rebounds and seven assists in a 122–102 victory over the [[2025–26 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=WSU alum have an explosive week in the NBA|url=https://dailyevergreen.com/192778/sports/pro-cougs-nba-coward-makes-history-as-gueye-dominates-lakers/|access-date=January 5, 2026|website=dailyevergreen.com|language=en}}</ref> On 9 February 2026, Gueye was ejected from a game against the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]] after being involved in an altercation with [[Naz Reid]] early in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Naz Reid, Mouhamed Gueye tossed after altercation late in game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47883208/naz-reid-mouhamed-gueye-tossed-altercation-late-game|access-date=March 31, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He and Reid were both subsequently fined $35,000 for the incident.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hawks’ Mouhamed Gueye, Wolves’ Naz Reid fined $35K for altercation|url=https://www.nba.com/news/mouhamed-gueye-naz-reid-fined-altercation|access-date=March 31, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 15 July 2026, it was announced that Gueye would be sidelined for three–to–four months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hawks forward Gueye has surgery for fractured left foot and could miss start of 2026-27 season|url=https://www.nba.com/news/mouhamed-gueye-surgery-could-miss-start-next-season|access-date=August 24, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref>
